sources.title: Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) - NCI
sources.why_relevant: Official NCI page defining CAM and listing cancer CAM clinical trials
sources.quote: Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) is the term for medical products and practices that are not part of standard medical care. People with cancer may use CAM to help cope with the side effects of cancer treatments, such as nausea, pain, and fatigue ... try to treat or cure their cancer

sources.title: Compound in North American Botanical Oplopanax horridus Inhibits Colorectal Tumor Growth in Mouse Model and Human Cells | NCCIH
sources.why_relevant: Official NCCIH page reporting a laboratory study of a natural product (oplopantriol A from Oplopanax horridus) against colorectal cancer
sources.quote: A new compound isolated from the Pacific Northwest shrub Oplopanax horridus, sometimes called Alaskan ginseng or devil's club, showed beneficial effects on human colorectal cells in a recent laboratory study. The study, funded in part by the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health ... was published in the journal Nutrients.

sources.title: Study Investigating the Ability of Plant Exosomes to Deliver Curcumin to Normal and Colon Cancer Tissue
sources.why_relevant: Official ClinicalTrials.gov record of a Phase I trial testing plant exosome-delivered curcumin (a natural product from turmeric) for colon cancer
sources.quote: This clinical trial will investigate the ability of plant exosomes to more effectively deliver curcumin to normal colon tissue and colon tumors. Curcumin is the yellow pigment of turmeric, a natural product with diverse biological activities.

sources.title: Division of Cancer Control and Population Sciences (DCCPS)
sources.why_relevant: Official NCI division page describing the US program for research into cancer causes, epidemiology, and prevention
sources.quote: Supporting research to better understand cancer causes and outcomes and to translate findings into clinical and public health interventions.
